topic.title: It’s SFT all the way down: learning Kaggriculture one action at a time

comments.content:
"To have money is to have power."

Thank you for sharing this perspective. It really resonated with me. 😆

I also participate in Kaggle competitions without any financial resources,
and I’d like to share what that experience has taught me and how it has shaped the way I think about competition.

I sometimes participate in Kaggle competitions, but my perspective has changed over time.
Rather than focusing only on rankings,
I now value the opportunity to learn new ideas and explore different approaches.

Because of this, I have come to define “winning” in a more personal way.
For me, success is not only about meeting external standards,
but also about achieving the goals I set for myself.

For example, if I study PPO and related algorithms, compare their behavior,
and gain a better understanding of what works and why,
I consider that meaningful progress.

This has also changed how I think about money.
I see money as an important and useful tool,
but not necessarily as a measure of personal value.
To me, value comes more from what we choose to pursue,
what we learn, and how we define our own goals.
